prediction.likelyOutcome: Lagoon should win on liability for the pre-termination unpaid rent ($364,212) and likely defeat the frustration-of-purpose defense as a matter of law, but the accelerated/future-rent component is unlikely to be fully resolved on this early summary-judgment motion given the genuine, document-supported mitigation dispute (the redevelopment/performance-venue evidence) and Landmark's pending request to depose Abdul before the discovery deadline. Expect partial summary judgment for Lagoon on unpaid rent and the frustration defense, with the penalty-doctrine and mitigation issues going to trial or a later motion, producing a total recovery below the full $1,808,470 demanded — most likely in the $950,000-$1,808,470 band depending on how the liquidated-damages and mitigation issues shake out.

outcome.description: The district court granted Lagoon summary judgment in June 2022, held the liquidated-damages clause enforceable so that no mitigation was required, and (after Lagoon waived attorney fees) entered judgment for $1,808,470 plus costs. The Minnesota Court of Appeals reversed on December 11, 2023, holding the liquidated-damages clause unenforceable because actual damages were capable of estimation and the clause ignored the duty to mitigate, and remanded for further proceedings on actual damages and mitigation.
outcome.finalNote: Reversed (liquidated-damages clause unenforceable) and remanded; no final figure yet.
